record.original_question: Construct a polarised surface (X, L) whose Seshadri constant at a very general point is irrational, or prove that the Seshadri constant on a surface is always rational.

evidence.quote: Construct a polarised surface (X, L) with irrational Seshadri constant at the very general point or prove that the Seshadri constant is always rational.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective surface and let $L$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. For a point $x \in X$, the Seshadri constant of $L$ at $x$ is defined by
$$\varepsilon(X,L;x) \;=\; \inf_{C \ni x} \frac{L \cdot C}{\mathrm{mult}_x C},$$
where the infimum runs over all irreducible curves $C \subset X$ passing through $x$. The Seshadri constant of $L$ at a very general point is the value $\varepsilon(X,L) := \varepsilon(X,L;x)$ for $x$ in the complement of a countable union of proper Zariski-closed subsets of $X$ (this common value exists).

Either:
(a) exhibit an explicit polarised smooth complex projective surface $(X,L)$ with $L$ ample such that $\varepsilon(X,L)$ at a very general point is an irrational real number; or
(b) prove that for every polarised smooth complex projective surface $(X,L)$, the Seshadri constant $\varepsilon(X,L)$ at a very general point is a rational number.
artifact.status_search_result: The rationality of Seshadri constants on surfaces at a very general point is a well-known long-standing open problem. All explicitly computed Seshadri constants to date are rational, but no unconditional example of irrationality is known. Recent works (e.g., on blow-ups of ruled surfaces and of P^2) establish rationality in special cases or produce irrational examples only conditionally on conjectures such as a strengthened SHGH conjecture. No unconditional resolution has been published as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Rationality of Seshadri constants on blow-ups of ruled surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Rationality of Seshadri constants is a long-standing open question, and although it is widely assumed to be false, there is no counterexample even in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is open; no counterexample is known.

status_evidence.title: A primer on Seshadri constants
status_evidence.snippet: All computed cases of Seshadri constants are rational... however, Seshadri constants on general surfaces of degree d≥5 are expected to be integral multiples of √d.
status_evidence.claim: Evidence is mixed and the rationality question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Rationality of Seshadri constants on general blow ups of P2
status_evidence.snippet: Assuming a strengthened SHGH conjecture, irrational Seshadri constants at a very general point can be exhibited.
status_evidence.claim: Only conditional progress on producing irrational Seshadri constants is available.
